VALMONT MÉTROPOLE · Direction des mobilités · Autorité organisatrice
Délégation de service public — Réseau Valmo · Contract DSP-VM-2021 (extracts)
Contract: DSP-VM-2021
Authority (délégant): Valmont Métropole
Operator (délégataire): Keolis Valmont SAS
Term: 1 January 2021 – 31 December 2028
Extension: One optional 2-year extension at the authority's discretion (not exercised)
Price basis: EUR, HT
Article 12 — Assets made available to the operator (biens de retour)
12.1 The rolling stock, depots, track, traction power installations, stations and systems listed in Annex 7 are owned by the Authority and made available to the Operator for the duration of the contract. They return to the Authority free of charge at the end of the contract (biens de retour).
12.2 The Operator keeps the inventory in Annex 7 current. Each line states the asset, its commissioning date and, for rolling stock, its contractual replacement date.
12.3 At handback the Operator delivers each asset with its maintenance records, open defects, spares, manuals and training material, in a condition consistent with normal wear.
Article 34 — Maintenance, major maintenance and renewal
34.1 Routine and preventive maintenance of every Annex 7 asset is the Operator's responsibility and is remunerated inside the contract price.
34.2 Major maintenance (gros entretien, GER) is borne by the Operator up to the per-intervention threshold in Annex 9 and is funded from the GER provision in the contract price.
34.3 Renewal and enhancement of assets are decided and funded by the Authority through its multi-year investment plan (PPI). Where the Authority delegates project management to the Operator, the Operator is reimbursed on quarterly claims supported by evidence of costs incurred and milestones achieved.
34.4 Where a vehicle remains in service after its contractual replacement date because the replacement has not been delivered, repairs to heavy components (engine, gearbox, traction battery) arising after that date are borne by the Authority, subject to the conditions in Avenant n°2.

Article 1 — Definitions
“Annex 7 assets” means the assets listed in Annex 7 as updated under Article 12.2. “Contractual replacement date” means the date stated for a vehicle in Annex 7, as amended. “GER” means major maintenance (gros entretien) as defined in Annex 9. “PPI” means the Authority's multi-year investment plan and the convention implementing it.
Article 10 — Service obligations
10.1 The Operator runs the service defined in Annex 3 (timetables, vehicle requirement by class, operating reserve). 10.2 The operating reserve is 10% of the peak requirement for 12 m buses, one vehicle for 18 m buses and two trams. 10.3 A planned withdrawal of service for works requires the Authority's prior approval of the access window and the substitution plan.
Article 35 — Delegated project management of renewals
35.1 Where the Authority delegates the management of a renewal project to the Operator, the delegation letter states the scope, the budget and the milestones. 35.2 The Operator claims reimbursement quarterly, within 15 days of quarter end, with evidence of costs incurred and milestones achieved (acceptance records, invoices). 35.3 Work funded from the GER provision cannot be claimed under the PPI.
Article 41 — Indexation
The contribution and the unit prices of Annex 9 are indexed annually on 1 January by the formula in Annex 10.
Article 45 — Penalties
45.1 A vehicle requirement not met at peak for reasons attributable to the Operator gives rise to a penalty of €1,200 per missing vehicle per day. 45.2 Late submission of the annual report under Article 48 gives rise to a penalty of €500 per day.
Article 48 — Annual report
The Operator submits the annual report of the delegate before 1 June each year, including the accounts of the delegation, the analysis of service quality, the Annex 7 inventory with its changes in the year and the renewal programme.

DOC:lessons-tranche1.text:
KEOLIS VALMONT SAS · Opérateur du Réseau Valmo · Direction technique et investissements
Post-project review — bus fleet renewal tranche 1 (2023–2024)
What happened
Tranche 1 (20 hybrid buses) was delivered 11 weeks late. Five buses were accepted with open defects and two had their release for duty delayed by missing insulation certificates.
Lessons
L1. Track the supplier's delivery promise from correspondence, not only from the ERP — the ERP promised date lagged the supplier's emails by an average of 19 days.
L2. Separate installed, accepted and duty-eligible counts in every status report. Reporting 'delivered' hid 7 vehicles that could not run.
L3. Notify the Authority under Article 34.4 as soon as a vehicle past its replacement date fails — two claims in 2024 were lost to the 30-day notice rule.

KEOLIS VALMONT SAS · Opérateur du Réseau Valmo · Direction technique et investissements
Engineering assessment — BUS-204 engine failure of 12 July 2026
Vehicle: BUS-204 (VIN VF7AR12D0B4000204), Arvéa Citybus 12 D, commissioned 1 July 2011
Failure: 12 July 2026 06:48 — loss of oil pressure, engine seized, line L07
Work order: WO-2026-071244
Odometer: 742,380 km
Diagnosis
Crankshaft bearing failure due to wear. Oil sample taken after failure shows fuel dilution. The 60,000 km oil-analysis task (OIL-60K) was due at 739,980 km and had not been carried out: overdue by 2,400 km.
Assessment
The failure is consistent with end-of-life wear. The engineering team cannot exclude that the overdue oil analysis would have detected the dilution. This question is referred to commercial review under Article 34.4.4.
Recommendation
Rebuild the engine (quote Q-26-1187, €28,000 HT) only if the vehicle is needed until tranche 2 batch 3 arrives; otherwise withdraw BUS-204.
